governanceNotes: D1 batch 62 (2026-09-26): identity deferred (CONSTITUTIVE-FEATURE-SET / IDENTITY-DUPLICATION with the hypothyroidism pathway). Myxedema coma is the rare decompensated emergency of severe hypothyroidism, and the located evidence supports no outgoing catalog edge: (i) the US National Inpatient Sample study of 2,495 myxedema-coma admissions (PMID 38279788) quantifies only in-hospital mortality (6.8 percent versus 0.7 percent; adjusted OR 9.92), length of stay, and cost - none of which is a catalog identity; (ii) the clinical features documented in the case literature (hypothermia, bradycardia, hypotension, altered sensorium, hypoventilation; PMID 41280597) are the diagnostic criteria of the syndrome itself (constitutive-proximity guard), so feature-directed edges would restate the presentation; (iii) the genuine complications described (multi-organ failure, delirium, respiratory failure, acute kidney injury) have no catalog identities and no condition-specific quantification in the located material; (iv) longer-term neurologic sequelae in the located case are confounded by pre-existing dementia and delirium; and (v) hypothyroidism-mediated pathways (anemia, cardiomyopathy, cognitive effects) belong to the published hypothyroidism identity's window - an edge from this emergency state would duplicate that scope (identity-duplication guard), and no evidence was recycled from it (ME-29). Reopening conditions: (a) a cohort quantifying a catalog-fit secondary diagnosis (e.g. an epilepsy or cardiomyopathy endpoint) in myxedema-coma survivors with baseline thyroid-status and comorbidity adjustment; or (b) a governance decision treating myxedema coma as an acute-care severity marker within the hypothyroidism identity rather than a standalone mapping source.

Direction discipline recorded 2026-09-26: the mortality and utilization endpoints in the anchor study are outcomes of the hospitalization, not secondary conditions of the syndrome; the seasonal and mortality signals are recorded here as context only.
